title: Candidate-Set Sampling in Temporal Job Recommendation: Cross-Dataset Evidence on  Model-Selection Agreement
content: Offline job-recommender evaluation often substitutes observed relevant jobs plus sampled alternatives for a large eligible catalog. This reduces scoring but can alter metrics and model-selection conclusions. We compare sampled and sampling-free, protocol-defined logged-catalog evaluation in a seven-window CareerBuilder backtest with 7,000 users and the JTH chronological task with 8,341 queries. Six CareerBuilder and seven JTH configurations were tested using nested uniform and popularity-weighted candidate sets across multiple sizes and five seeds. At size 100, HitRate@20 inflation for BM25, term frequency–inverse document frequency (TF–IDF), and MiniLM ranged from 0.6137 to 0.8636 in CareerBuilder and 0.4730 to 0.6409 in JTH. JTH sampling reversed the sampling-free BM25–MiniLM ordering; CareerBuilder retained full-text BM25 as top-ranked but compressed its contrast with TF–IDF. Mean average precision at cutoff 20 (MAP@20) favored BM25 under all displayed protocols. Agreement generally improved with candidate fraction, yet 10,000 CareerBuilder candidates represented only 8.4734% of the mean eligible catalog and did not recover the complete ordering. A CPU-only direct-scoring benchmark confirmed substantial reductions in scoring and ranking work. These findings establish candidate-set construction as a decision-relevant component of temporal job-recommender evaluation and support calibration against eligible-catalog references.
